stories.headline: Canada’s military names the four soldiers killed in the CFB Wainwright fire, which began as a grass fire during live-fire combat training
stories.summary: The Canadian Armed Forces on Sunday identified the four service members killed in Saturday’s fire at CFB Wainwright in Alberta: Sgt. Morgan Wong of Edmonton, Pte. Shaun Farrell of Prince Albert, Sask., Pte. Aidan Goulding of North Vancouver, B.C., and Pte. Hayden Lykkemark of Langley, B.C. All four served with the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry out of CFB Edmonton. Maj.-Gen. Wade Rutland said the unit was doing “high intensity combat training with live munitions” to prepare as a global response task force and for a deployment to Latvia next spring when a grass fire ignited in the training area. Uncommonly strong winds, with gusts up to 100 km/h across the province, drove it rapidly toward the range’s administrative area; the cause is under investigation. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people remain in hospital, at least 19 in critical condition. “It is with heavy hearts that we share the news that our son, Shaun Farrell, has passed away,” his mother wrote on Facebook.

stories.headline: Mexico charges Chihuahua’s former attorney general with treason for working with U.S. agencies, including the CIA, against the cartels
stories.summary: Mexico’s federal Attorney General’s Office has arrested Cesar Jauregui, the former attorney general of the border state of Chihuahua, and Attorney General Ernestina Godoy says he is charged with treason in matters of national security. The case isn’t about corruption or cartel ties. It centers on Chihuahua working directly with U.S. agencies, chiefly the CIA, without federal approval, an effort that led to the discovery in April of one of the largest clandestine drug labs in Mexico’s history. Two U.S. agents and top Chihuahua law enforcement officials later died in a crash while returning from the lab site, which prompted President Claudia Sheinbaum to insist only the federal government may coordinate with foreign officials and to call for an investigation. Jauregui resigned in April and took the blame, partly shielding the state’s National Action Party governor. Breitbart Texas notes the contrast with Sheinbaum’s defense of Morena politicians the U.S. has accused of cartel ties.

stories.headline: An Irvine real estate agent is indicted as an unregistered Chinese agent, accused of surveilling the Taiwanese president’s son outside his Seattle-area home
stories.summary: Wanying “Heather” Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, has been indicted in federal court in Los Angeles on charges of conspiracy and acting as an unregistered agent of China. Prosecutors say that between roughly June and September 2025, at the direction of a Chinese government official who was her former classmate at the University of International Relations, a school an FBI investigator called “closely affiliated with China’s intelligence apparatus,” she flew to the Seattle area to watch a son of Taiwan’s president outside his home, sending photos, video and license plate details back to her handler. She also allegedly traveled to China in August 2025 to meet an official. Her lawyer has called the government’s sleeper-agent theory unsupported, describing her as a real estate agent raising two young daughters. A judge ordered her held as a flight risk; she is due for arraignment Friday and faces up to 15 years in prison.

stories.headline: The Amelia Earhart expedition to Nikumaroro comes up empty: the “Taraia Object” in the lagoon was most likely a pile of washed-up trees
stories.summary: A Purdue-backed expedition that sailed five days to the remote Pacific island of Nikumaroro to examine a satellite anomaly that some hoped was Amelia Earhart’s Lockheed Electra announced Sunday that it was not the plane. “Evidence gathered at the Taraia Peninsula on Nikumaroro confirmed that the visual anomaly first seen in satellite imagery in 2020 was likely a collection of large trees deposited along the peninsula’s sandspit,” the researchers said; by the time they arrived, most of the debris had broken up and washed away, leaving a single Y-shaped segment. The 17-member team, led by Purdue’s Steve Schultz and the Archaeological Legacy Institute’s Richard Pettigrew, launched Oct. 14, but severe weather kept them aboard ship for three of their five days and limited fuel kept them from staying longer. The team had earlier called the evidence “very strong.” Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished on July 2, 1937, and the latest letdown follows a 2024 sonar “plane” that turned out to be a rock formation.

stories.headline: An EU filing reveals the iPhone Duo’s battery: 4,883mAh across two cells, right between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max
stories.summary: With iPhone Duo pre-orders open, Apple has posted an EU regulatory document that finally reveals the foldable’s true battery capacity: 4,883mAh, split between a 2,962mAh cell and a 1,921mAh cell. That lands almost exactly between the iPhone 18 Pro (4,288mAh) and the iPhone 18 Pro Max (5,567mAh), 9to5Mac reports, making it one of the largest batteries Apple has ever put in an iPhone; only the two most recent Pro Max models beat it. The site cautions that capacity is not the same as battery life, since heavy use of the Duo’s larger inner display will drain it faster than a conventional slab phone.

stories.headline: Penguins close their road trip Monday in Utah after a 6-2 rout in Vegas, with three straight losses and five-plus goals allowed in each
stories.summary: The Penguins wrap up a four-game road trip Monday night in Salt Lake City against the Utah Mammoth, with both teams coming off identical 6-2 losses on Saturday, Pittsburgh in Las Vegas and Utah at home to Edmonton. The loss to Vegas was Pittsburgh’s third straight and its sixth in seven games (1-5-1) after a 2-0 start, and the Penguins have given up at least five goals in each of the first three games of the trip. “We can’t be feeling bad for ourselves. It’s on all of us, myself included,” coach Dan Muse said. “There’s a lot coming off of (Saturday) night that we have to clean up from a structural standpoint.” The Golden Knights scored three even-strength goals in the first period before Sidney Crosby’s power-play goal made it 3-1. Ahead of the game the Penguins recalled defenseman Ilya Solovyov from Wilkes-Barre/Scranton and sent Ryan Johnson down. The teams meet again Oct. 29 in Pittsburgh.

stories.headline: Ex-Kentucky cheerleader Laken Snelling gets 10 years for killing her newborn son and hiding him in a trash bag in her closet
stories.summary: Former University of Kentucky cheerleader Laken Snelling, 22, was sentenced to ten years in prison for killing her newborn son, after pleading guilty in August to first-degree manslaughter, concealing the birth of an infant, tampering with physical evidence and abuse of a corpse. She will have to serve 85 percent of the sentence before parole eligibility and cannot get probation. At sentencing the court heard the baby had been named McCoy Cade Hall; one relative said the family had looked forward to “first words, kisses, and all the little moments,” and that “for Cade, those possibilities were taken away.” Snelling had admitted in court, “Instead of helping him I ended his life and afterwards I cleaned up and didn’t tell anyone.” Lexington police found the baby on Aug. 27, 2025, wrapped in a towel inside a trash bag in a closet of her off-campus home after roommates called 911. The medical examiner ruled he was born alive and died of asphyxia, and police said she had deleted photos taken during labor to hide the birth.

stories.headline: Macron addresses France after Saturday’s riots, blames far-left extremists and “criminals,” and asks “How can French people do this to France?”
stories.summary: In his first address to the nation since the youth protest movement began nearly a month ago, French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday evening blamed “extremists from far-left groups” and “criminals” for Saturday’s nationwide riots, which torched historic buildings, saw thousands of shops looted and injured hundreds of police officers, gendarmes and firefighters. “Why burn down the town hall in Limoges, the tourist office in Lyon, storm the town hall in Marseille, or attack the prefect’s residence in Bordeaux?” he asked. “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it.” Macron said the hundreds of thousands who marched over the cost of living and fuel prices had legitimate concerns, tied Europe’s energy crunch to the U.S.–Iran conflict, and said he will travel to the Gulf on Monday to secure fuel supplies. He has ordered his interior and justice ministers to review the response, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will chair a crisis meeting Monday on aid for business owners, with some costs to be recovered from convicted rioters. Breitbart notes he did not address immigration. Marine Le Pen said millions of angry French people “are not breaking anything,” Jordan Bardella called it a “lamentable speech,” and Éric Zemmour blamed the arrival of “500,000 foreigners a year for the past 10 years.”

stories.headline: A priest in Ecuador is killed when a large wooden crucifix falls on him as he prepares Communion during a livestreamed Mass
stories.summary: Father Patricio Alfredo Sánchez Molinari was standing at the altar of Nuestra Señora del Perpetuo Socorro Church in Guayaquil, Ecuador, preparing Communion on Saturday when the large wooden crucifix behind him suddenly fell forward and struck him, Fox News reports. The Mass was being livestreamed on social media, and the video captures screams as worshippers rushed to his side, with a woman heard shouting, “Father, Father … call an ambulance.” The Archdiocese of Guayaquil confirmed his death in a Facebook statement, identifying him as the parish priest of Perpetuo Socorro in its Central Vicariate; the day before, the archdiocese had congratulated him on the anniversary of his ordination, according to the Ecuadorian outlet Primicias. Sánchez Molinari was a member of the Redemptorists and previously spent several years as parish priest at San Lorenzo in Vinces, in Los Ríos province, where his former parish posted a tribute. Church officials had not explained what caused the crucifix to fall as of Sunday.

stories.headline: Trump defends his Russia sanctions waiver and diesel deal on Truth Social and tears into Zelensky: “I WANT THIS WAR END!”
stories.summary: President Trump used a Truth Social post on Sunday to defend his recent moves on Russia, including waiving sanctions, a deal for Russia to release diesel onto world markets and pressure on Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries. “My decision on Russia is a very simple one,” he wrote. “I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” adding that “great progress is being made,” including on hostage negotiations. Trump argued that Russia is doing “very little, if anything” to help Iran in its war with the U.S. and is instead “sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World,” and he accused Zelensky of targeting Russian diesel refineries “knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States.” He went on to say Zelensky could have made a better deal two years ago: “His country is in shambles, a large portion of his land is lost, his oceans and seas are gone, and his male population is low, wounded, and/or dead.” The Kyiv Independent notes that the moves have alarmed Kyiv as Russian strikes continue, and that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has insisted the sanctions were only waived, not lifted.

stories.headline: A cattle truck plunges off a Kansas City overpass, killing up to 60 cows and sending dozens more wandering the city’s highways
stories.summary: A semitrailer hauling 120 to 130 head of cattle overturned on the westbound I-70 curve in downtown Kansas City, Missouri, shortly before 3 a.m. Sunday and fell onto southbound I-35, landing on a car, CBS News reports. Both drivers had minor injuries and were treated at local hospitals. Kansas City police Sgt. Phil DiMartino said between 45 and 60 of the cattle were killed, while dozens of others fled the scene, causing more crashes and a flood of calls to police; some walked several miles before they were caught. The city launched drones to track the animals until a private company working with the trucking firm arrived with workers on horseback to round them up, and by Sunday afternoon police said all the cows were believed to be accounted for. Fire Battalion Chief Michael Hopkins said recovering the animals that didn’t survive had been the harder job. The crash came on the day the Chiefs hosted the Chargers at Arrowhead, though officials did not expect major game-day traffic problems.

stories.headline: A London councillor wants Marilyn Manson pulled from Slipknot’s Wembley Stadium show, and Jim Root says booking support acts isn’t his call
stories.summary: Marilyn Manson is booked to support Slipknot at Wembley Stadium on July 3, 2027, the opening night of their (sic)est stadium tour, on a bill with Lorna Shore and Hatebreed, but Brent Council Liberal Democrat leader Anton Georgiou has called on the venue to reconsider because of sexual misconduct allegations against the singer, which Manson denies. “The allegations against Marilyn Manson are serious, and while he denies wrongdoing, Wembley Stadium needs to explain what consideration was given to them before this booking was confirmed,” Georgiou said. Brent Council replied that bookings are a matter for the venue and promoters, not the council, and Wembley said support acts are chosen by the promoter and headliner and that it is in talks with Live Nation about the performance. Slipknot guitarist Jim Root posted that the decision had nothing to do with him: “I concentrate on writing and being a guitarist, so forgive my ignorance about who we do shows with.” Manson, who is also slated for four South American dates on the tour, is scheduled to stand trial in November 2027 in a sexual assault and battery lawsuit brought by his former assistant Ashley Walters, Louder reports.

stories.headline: Trump gives Netanyahu his “Complete and Total Endorsement” ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 election, warning that anyone else would leave America to do the work on Iran
stories.summary: President Trump publicly endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud Party on Sunday ahead of Israel’s Oct. 27 Knesset elections, calling him a “great warrior” and America’s partner amid the multi-front war against Iran. “I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times,” Trump wrote. “Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure — But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger.” He called the post a letter of “Complete and Total Endorsement” and added a warning: “If Israel has the wrong leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so.” Netanyahu replied on X shortly after: “Thank you, President Trump, for the tremendous support and the joint work. Together, we will complete the mission.” Israelis vote for party lists, and the next prime minister needs the backing of at least 61 of the Knesset’s 120 members. Fox says current forecasts have Likud winning roughly 18 to 22 seats and Netanyahu’s right-religious bloc about 49 to 51, short of a majority, which would leave smaller parties holding the balance of power.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.

stories.headline: Jets fall 26-19 in Foxborough as stalled drives and Geno Smith’s first interception waste Omar Cooper Jr.’s 48-yard touchdown
stories.summary: The Jets hung around at Gillette Stadium on Sunday but lost 26-19 to the Patriots, their 15th loss in their last 16 games in Foxborough and fourth in five games overall, dropping Aaron Glenn’s team to 2-4 while New England moved to 4-2. Playing without Breece Hall, the Jets opened with a 13-play drive that ended in a 42-yard Jason Sanders field goal after an 11-yard Smith touchdown pass to Omar Cooper Jr. was wiped out by an offensive pass interference call on Tim Patrick. From there the offense stalled: back-to-back sacks set up a 42-yard Drake Maye touchdown pass to Romeo Doubs, and two straight drives died on fourth down, with Braelon Allen, who had 65 rushing yards by halftime, stopped on fourth-and-2 and Smith stuffed on fourth-and-1, as New England built a 17-3 halftime lead. The Jets rallied in the third quarter when Smith hit a wide-open Cooper for a 48-yard touchdown, David Bailey forced a TreVeyon Henderson fumble that Jamien Sherwood recovered, and Sanders added a field goal to make it 17-13. But Maye found Hunter Henry for his third touchdown pass, Smith threw his first interception of the season early in the fourth, and after a Sherwood forced fumble led to another field goal, a 13-play Patriots drive ended in a field goal with 1:12 left. A fourth Jets field goal made it 26-19 with 32 seconds to go, but New England recovered the onside kick.

stories.headline: Wichita police name the boy and man killed on the soccer field and release the driver without charges while they wait on toxicology tests
stories.summary: Wichita police on Sunday identified the two people killed when a pickup truck drove onto a youth soccer field at the Stryker Sports Complex on Saturday afternoon as 6-year-old Cole Adrian and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer. Both were from McPherson, Kansas, but were not related. The driver, a 34-year-old woman from Garden City, was questioned and has been released with no charges filed for now, pending the results of a toxicology report and an inspection of the truck. Police say a preliminary investigation shows she had been parked in a space near the fields before driving onto one of them and hitting multiple people. Two of her children were in the pickup and were also interviewed, and another of her children was playing on a different field at the complex. Ten people, ages 5 to 68 and including two 5-year-olds, two 8-year-olds and a 9-year-old, were hospitalized with injuries described as noncritical; an 11th person, a 61-year-old woman, was taken to the hospital with unrelated medical complications. “What should have been a day of children playing soccer and families spending time together ended in tragedy,” Police Chief Joe Sullivan said. All events at the complex are canceled until further notice, and police are asking anyone with video or photos to share them.

stories.headline: NATO jets scramble as a likely drone explodes over northern Lithuania, hours after a foiled arson attempt on a Starlink site that Lithuania calls Russian sabotage
stories.summary: An unidentified flying object, likely a drone, entered Lithuanian airspace and exploded on Sunday, sending residents to shelters and damaging a civilian vehicle, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda said. NATO fighter jets were scrambled but could not identify the object in cloudy weather and did not try to shoot it down; it later dropped off radar, and officials examined what appeared to be drone debris near the village of Juodzionys in northern Lithuania. No one was hurt. Lithuania’s defense minister said the drone came in from Poland, though Poland’s defense ministry said its radar did not confirm it crossing the border, according to Reuters. A Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesman said Russian electronic warfare may have diverted Ukrainian drones off course and apologized for “any disruption, risks, and concern.” Earlier Sunday, Lithuanian authorities foiled an overnight attempt to set fire to a company storing Starlink satellite equipment. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said he believes Russian actors commissioned it, and the head of Lithuania’s crisis management center called it sabotage tied to earlier Starlink arsons in Bulgaria and Poland and aimed at Ukraine. The day before, Romanian jets shot down two Shahed-style drones in Romanian airspace.

stories.headline: William Shatner, 95, fronts a heavy metal band and is making an album with 50-plus metal musicians, including a Brian May guitar solo
stories.summary: William Shatner says his reaction when his label, Cleopatra Records, pitched him a heavy metal album earlier this year became its title: “What the F Is Heavy Metal.” The 95-year-old “Star Trek” star told Fox News Digital he wrote six original songs with longtime collaborator Robert Sharenow and that more than 50 metal musicians volunteered to play on the record, including Queen’s Brian May, who contributed a guitar solo to “Rage,” a track built around Dylan Thomas’ line “Rage, rage against the dying of the light.” A title track is due out this winter. Shatner’s band, The *uckers, debuted in Chicago on Sept. 19 and played Riot Fest the next day, mixing originals like “Rage,” “Sky” and “One Fear” with covers of “Crazy Train,” “Ace of Spades” and “Enter Sandman.” He says the Riot Fest reception “proved to me the viability” of the project, and that his take on “Enter Sandman” is “a total reinterpretation” focused on the song’s darker side. His answer to his own question now: heavy metal “is the beat of life.” Shatner, who has tinnitus that he traces to a “Star Trek” explosion scene, says the loud music can temporarily make the ringing worse.

stories.headline: Judas Priest open “The Early Years,” an interactive online scrapbook of the Rocka Rolla and Sad Wings of Destiny era
stories.summary: Exciter Records has launched “The Early Years,” an interactive online Judas Priest scrapbook covering the band’s formative period around 1974’s “Rocka Rolla” and 1976’s “Sad Wings of Destiny,” with early photos, videos and memorabilia. The site doubles as the hub for this year’s 50th-anniversary editions of “Sad Wings,” the album that gave fans “Victim of Changes,” “The Ripper,” “Tyrant” and “Dreamer Deceiver.” Exciter and its publishing affiliate Reach Music, working with the band, acquired the album’s master rights, returning control of it to Priest and its partners. There are two versions, both restoring the band’s intended track order opening with “Prelude”: “Original 1976 Masters,” remastered from the original analog tapes, which came out Oct. 2 on streaming and Oct. 9 on CD and vinyl and adds the original 1976 recording of “Diamonds and Rust,” and a new “Remixed & Remastered” edition produced by Tom Allom with the same team that remixed “Rocka Rolla,” which is streaming now and arrives as a half-speed-mastered double LP and CD on Nov. 27. “ ‘Sad Wings of Destiny’ was a defining moment for us as a band,” Priest said in a statement. Rob Halford has called it his personal favorite Priest album.

stories.headline: Abdul El-Sayed admits his sister-in-law was on the federal terrorist watchlist under Obama, days before Obama campaigns with him in Michigan
stories.summary: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed acknowledged Saturday night that his sister-in-law, Mariam Jukaku, had been on the federal terrorist watchlist during the Obama administration, but said she was removed in 2016. Fox News correspondent Mike Tobin confronted him in a hallway about court papers naming Jukaku as a plaintiff in a 2016 lawsuit challenging her placement in the Terrorist Screening Dataset; the suit says she went through extensive airport screening in 2012 without ever being told she had been flagged. “She did nothing wrong and was captured on that and then sued and got off,” El-Sayed said, blaming a system where people are “guilty until proven innocent because they’ve got different kinds of names” and the “infrastructure that people like Mike Rogers set up,” referring to his Republican opponent. The record is murkier than his answer: a federal appeals court overturned the ruling that had favored Jukaku and the other plaintiffs in 2021, and a separate damages suit was dismissed in 2017. The government says it neither confirms nor denies anyone’s inclusion on the list, and Fox notes the lawsuit does not establish wrongdoing by Jukaku or El-Sayed. The admission is awkward timing, since Barack Obama is scheduled to campaign with El-Sayed in Michigan on Oct. 24, and it comes after weeks of attacks over alleged family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, which his campaign calls racist and untrue.
